text:
sanjay: heads-up — seeing a sharp p99 latency spike on dedicated-us-east-1-g1 starting ~07:42 UTC. correlating with a kernel-selector change that flipped to the avx512 path at ~07:40. batch window decay & kv hit-rate dropped around the same time.

sanjay: quick dump from profiler (trimmed):
```
pool: dedicated-us-east-1-g1
time: 2026-03-18T07:42:10Z
metric: dispatch_ms=18.3 -> 34.9
batch_avg_tokens=6.2 -> 3.1
kvcache_hits=0.73 -> 0.41
noisy_tenant_top=tenant-t-4513 (20% of requests)
```

incident-bot: created INC-2026-0421 for the latency spike (severity: high). paging on-call.

elaine: acknowledged. any recent rollout besides kernel-selector?

sanjay: only selector flip and a minor batching heuristic tweak (batch-window decay: 250ms -> 120ms) in the same push. suspect interaction between avx512 kernels and short batches -> kernel dispatch overhead dominates and kv entries are getting evicted (kv-shadowing) causing miss storms.

maya: sounds like noisy neighbor amplification. we should try two quick mitigations in parallel: 1) throttle tenant-t-4513 to 2rps, 2) revert kernel-selector on that pool to avx2. whichever is faster.

ryan: I can toggle a feature flag for the tenant throttle: `feature/tenant-rate-limiter/t-4513` -> set to 2rps. applying now.

ops-bot: feature flag `feature/tenant-rate-limiter/t-4513` enabled (2rps) on dedicated-us-east-1-g1 by ryan.

sanjay: rolling kernel-selector rollback for the pool: setting `kernel_selector.override=avx2` on pool-level. will watch health.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0421 updated: mitigation actions started (throttle + selector rollback).

qa-jordan: running quick synthetic checks against the pool. baseline p99 before incident ~ 420ms. current p99 after throttle+rollback (30s) = 260ms — trending down.

elaine: good. can we also enable fallback routing for new sessions to the quantized-but-stable variant (gptx-small-q4) for 5 minutes as a protective measure?

sanjay: enabling route fallback policy: `route-policy: prefer(gptx-prod) -> fallback(gptx-small-q4) if latency>300ms` for 5m on that shard. done.

ops-bot: route-policy applied on shard s-east-1-02 for 5m by sanjay.

maya: while this stabilizes, we should capture a full perf trace: enable flameprof on 3 replicas and increase kv cache retention for the pool to avoid eviction noise (kv_retention=60s -> 180s).

ryan: flameprof started (3 replicas). also bumped kv_retention to 180s on the pool.

sanjay: grabbing heap of dispatch traces and kernel timings. early look shows AVX512 path has a 2.1x dispatch overhead for short sequences vs avx2 due to extra prologue work. when batch sizes shrink below ~4 tokens the overhead dominates. combined with shorter batch-window we saw median batch size collapse -> cascade of kv misses (kv-shadowing).

elaine: lesson: selector heuristics need to account for observed batch-size distribution and kv cache pressure. file a follow-up for a selector probe that samples runtime batch sizes and forces kernel choice per-quantile.

sanjay: created follow-up ticket INF-2026-798: "selector-probe: sample runtime batch-size quantiles and choose kernel for p99 latency minima" with links to traces.

qa-jordan: p99 now stable ~230ms, p95 ~85ms. throughput at pool steady, no tail-growth.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0421 severity downgraded to medium. documenting mitigations: tenant throttle, kernel-selector rollback, route fallback, kv_retention bump.

maya: next steps: 1) revert temporary tenant throttle after 15m if things look good, 2) run a controlled canary of a selector that prefers avx2 for short batches but avx512 for long sequences, 3) add a kv cache metric alert for kv_hit_rate < 0.5.

ryan: I will schedule the canary and the kv alert. tagging infra for kernel build analysis.

elaine: thanks all — great quick coordination. add a short postmortem note in /incidents when you have the trace links. :thumbsup:

sanjay: will add traces + perf diffs to the incident doc. rolling back feature/tenant-rate-limiter/t-4513 now (15m window elapsed).

ops-bot: feature flag `feature/tenant-rate-limiter/t-4513` disabled by sanjay.

qa-jordan: final check: p99 after unthrottling remains ~240ms (within acceptable range). closing loop for now.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0421 resolved (final severity: medium). mitigation summary attached.

sanjay: follow-up owners: selector probe (sanjay), kv alert (ryan), canary + perf tests (maya).
